title: FILTER ( Sales, ... ) as a filter argument is evaluated in the outer context and overwrites the row's own filter
query: EVALUATE ADDCOLUMNS ( VALUES ( Product[Color] ), "Amount", CALCULATE ( [Sales Amount], FILTER ( Sales, Sales[Quantity] > 1 ) ) )

source.quote: the formula returns the same value for all the rows
source.supports: the article's query: every row gets the same value

source.quote: the filter parameters of CALCULATE are evaluated in the original filter context, not in the one that CALCULATE is about to produce
source.supports: the FILTER runs before context transition, over all of Sales

source.quote: when you place a filter on Sales, it results in applying the filter not only on the Sales table, but also on the Product table
source.supports: its result carries Product[Color], which overwrites the color of the current row

derivation: FILTER ( Sales, Quantity > 1 ) is evaluated with no color filter: rows 2 (40), 4 (50), 5 (200), 6 (30). As an expanded table it includes Product[Color], so it replaces the filter that context transition put on the color. Every row: 40 + 50 + 200 + 30 = 320.
